extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers / novelists seeking craft guidance on pacing
extracted.subtask_description: Advice and evaluative criteria for controlling the pace of a novel or long-form fiction, including when to use scene vs. summary, techniques to speed up or slow down, common pacing failures, and genre-specific expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of pacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Pacing = the rate at which narrative events, information, and emotional experiences are delivered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not just speed; rhythm — alternation between tension/release, density/space, action/reflection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scene vs. Summary (the Master Lever)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scene — events rendered in real time with dialogue, sensory detail, action; slow but immersive. Summary — events condensed into narration; fast but distancing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All-scene novels = bloated; all-summary novels = emotionally remote. Quality fiction calibrates per moment; use scene to dramatize crucial moments and summary to compress less important stretches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short sentences and paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: Use short sentences and short paragraphs to increase perceived speed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short, clipped syntax accelerates reading and heightens urgency; useful in action, pursuit, or high-tension moments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short chapters
rubrics_metrics.description: Make chapters short to create a faster rhythm and encourage page-turning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short chapters can sustain momentum and allow frequent transitions or cliffhanger placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heavy dialogue (less description)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rely on dialogue rather than descriptive exposition to speed the pace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dialogue moves events forward quickly and reduces narrative density; good for scenes that should feel brisk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active verbs
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer active verbs to make sentences leaner and more immediate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active voice often reads faster and gives scenes forward motion; reduces passive, distancing constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cut to the next scene mid-action
rubrics_metrics.description: Transition out of a scene in the middle of action to maintain momentum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaving a scene mid-action can quicken pacing and create urgency; pair with chapter breaks or cuts to other threads for tension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate transitional summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove unnecessary transitional summarizing to keep the narrative moving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid filler bridging scenes with bland summary; move directly to consequential moments instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cliffhangers between chapters
rubrics_metrics.description: End chapters on unresolved beats to propel the reader forward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective in genres seeking high momentum (e.g., thrillers); overuse can exhaust readers, so balance with relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Longer, more complex sentences
rubrics_metrics.description: Use extended, complex sentences to slow the pace and create weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complex syntax invites closer reading and can stretch time over a moment, appropriate for introspection or description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed sensory description
rubrics_metrics.description: Pause to supply rich sensory detail to decelerate the narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lingering on smells, textures, sounds, and visuals enlarges a moment and deepens immersion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interior reflection
rubrics_metrics.description: Extend moments of character thought and feeling to slow and deepen scenes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interiority allows readers to experience emotional stakes; use when emotional resonance matters more than forward plot motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flashback and contextualization
rubrics_metrics.description: Use flashbacks and contextual detail to expand temporal scope and slow movement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flashbacks enlarge a moment's significance but can stall forward momentum if overused; integrate deliberately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lingering on a single image or moment
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus closely on a single image or instant to create a slowed, textured effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Zooming in on micro-details elongates perceived time and deepens atmosphere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scene with low overt conflict but rich texture
rubrics_metrics.description: Include scenes that are not high-conflict but offer texture and mood to decelerate and vary rhythm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to provide breathing room and deepen characterization; avoid making them feel irrelevant to the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match pacing to content
rubrics_metrics.description: Align the speed of narration to the nature of the content (e.g., emotional climax slow; chase scene fast).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pacing should enhance the thematic and emotional logic of scenes; mismatches (rushed climax or languid chase) weaken impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vary the rhythm
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternate tempo across the work so that readers experience contrasts between fast and slow passages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relentless sprint exhausts; unbroken stroll bores. Deliberate variation maintains interest and emotional contour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pace shifts must be deliberate
rubrics_metrics.description: Transitions between speeds should be intentional and well-executed to preserve immersion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sloppy transitions break the dream; use clear narrative choices (cuts, time markers, tonal cues) when changing pace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading-aloud test
rubrics_metrics.description: Read prose aloud to evaluate whether pacing 'feels right' to the ear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cadence, sentence length, and rhythm become apparent when spoken; use this as a diagnostic for awkward or wrong pacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic compression / expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: Most stories are 90% summary collapsed into 10% scene; compress and expand strategically to shape focus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide which moments deserve scene-level treatment and which can be summarized; keep the 10% of scenes that carry the story's emotional and plot weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saggy middles (second-act problems)
rubrics_metrics.description: A common failure where the middle of a novel loses momentum and interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagnose saggy middles by looking for lack of escalating stakes or insufficient scene-level moments; tighten, add obstacles, or redistribute key scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endless setup; story starts too late
rubrics_metrics.description: Excessive setup that delays the real story (e.g., nothing significant happens until page 50).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with a compelling inciting incident or compress backstory; eliminate irrelevant exposition that postpones the story's thrust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climactic scene rushed
rubrics_metrics.description: Rushing the climax so it lacks emotional payoff or clear resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expand climactic scenes into full scenes with sensory detail and stakes rather than summarizing them; ensure proper buildup beforehand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aftermath dragged out
rubrics_metrics.description: Extending the aftermath of events longer than necessary, diluting momentum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclude consequences concisely once emotional and plot needs are met; avoid repetitive or aimless denouement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue scenes that should be summarized
rubrics_metrics.description: Overlong or aimless dialogue that could be condensed into summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If dialogue doesn't advance plot or deepen character, consider summarizing to maintain pace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary scenes that should be dramatized
rubrics_metrics.description: Important moments are handled as summary when they deserve scene-level dramatization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elevate pivotal beats into scenes with dialogue and sensory detail to increase emotional impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thriller pacing expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Thriller — high pace, short chapters, frequent cliffhangers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use rapid cuts, relentless escalation, and structural hooks to sustain tension and compel reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary pacing expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Literary — variable, often deliberate slow stretches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow longer reflective or descriptive passages; prioritize depth over relentless momentum while maintaining purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Romance pacing expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Romance — alternating intimate scene with separation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance scenes of closeness with obstacles/separation to create rhythm and emotional stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Horror pacing expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Horror — slow build interrupted by quick shocks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sustain dread through slower accumulation of detail and then punctuate with sudden, swift jolts to maximize fright.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy pacing expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedy — escalating absurdity; rhythm of jokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage timing and escalation so jokes land and build on one another; pacing controls setup and punchline tempo.
